Booker T. Washington, Up from Slavery.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/booker-t-washington/up-from-slavery

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Booker T. Washington, the author, the dedicatee, the writer of a preface, died 1915 (Wikidata Q319871, P570 = 1915-11-14).
- Walter H. Page, the annotator, the writer of an introduction, died 1918 (Wikidata Q1428445, P570 = 1918-12-22).

First publication of the text used: 1901 (SE colophon: 'Up from Slavery was published in 1901 by Booker T. Washington.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in the United States in 1901, before 1931. A work first published in the United States before 1931 is in the United States public domain (rights statement below).
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published there in 1901 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up_from_Slavery, country: United States). The United States rule settles its origin, whatever the death year of any person named above.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
